simvastatin.t: Avoid simvastatin and lovastatin doses greater than 40 mg [see Clinical Pharmacology ( 12.3 )].
( 7.3 ) Patients receiving more than 40 mg per day of simvastatin or lovastatin, or more than 20 mg per day of rosuvastatin may be at increased risk of statin related adverse effects.

digoxin.t: ( 7.4 ) Monitor digoxin levels with initiation of or any change in ticagrelor tablets.
7.5 Digoxin Ticagrelor tablets inhibits the P-glycoprotein transporter; monitor digoxin levels with initiation of or change in ticagrelor tablets therapy [see Clinical Pharmacology ( 12.3 )].

heparin.t: False negative platelet functional test results have been reported for Heparin Induced Thrombocytopenia (HIT).

5.7 Laboratory Test Interferences False negative functional tests for Heparin Induced Thrombocytopenia (HIT) Ticagrelor tablets have been reported to cause false negative results in platelet functional tests (including the heparin-induced platelet aggregation (HIPA) assay) for patients with Heparin Induced Thrombocytopenia (HIT).

antiplt.t: BLEEDING RISK Ticagrelor tablets, like other antiplatelet agents, can cause significant, sometimes fatal bleeding ( 5.1 , 6.1 ).

cyp3a4_inh.t: 7 DRUG INTERACTIONS Avoid use with strong CYP3A inhibitors or CYP3A inducers.

Avoid use of strong inhibitors of CYP3A (e.g., ketoconazole, itraconazole, voriconazole, clarithromycin, nefazodone, ritonavir, saquinavir, nelfinavir, indinavir, atazanavir and telithromycin) [see Clinical Pharmacology ( 12.3 )].

cyp3a4_ind.t: 7 DRUG INTERACTIONS Avoid use with strong CYP3A inhibitors or CYP3A inducers.
7.2 Strong CYP3A Inducers Strong CYP3A inducers substantially reduce ticagrelor exposure and so decrease the efficacy of ticagrelor.

statin.t: Avoid simvastatin and lovastatin doses greater than 40 mg [see Clinical Pharmacology ( 12.3 )].
Avoid rosuvastatin doses greater than 20 mg [see Clinical Pharmacology ( 12.3 )] .

opioid.t: 7.3 Opioids As with other oral P2Y12 inhibitors, co-administration of opioid agonists delay and reduce the absorption of ticagrelor and its active metabolite presumably because of slowed gastric emptying [ see Clinical Pharmacology ( 12.3 ) ].
Consider the use of a parenteral anti-platelet agent in acute coronary syndrome patients requiring co-administration of morphine or other opioid agonists.
